_readme: THE EGRESS LEDGER. Every host reached by networking implemented in this repo
is enumerated here, and here ONLY. Installed provider clients are a narrower
exception: their vendor-controlled supporting host set is not implemented or
pinned by this repo, so their root service destinations and boundary are
recorded here without pretending an external binary's internals are ours.
This file exists because the same claim used to be written out
longhand in nine prose files -- ui/AGENTS.md, connectors/AGENTS.md,
README.md, four sections of site/privacy/index.html, connect/lib/status.mjs,
widget/ui/connections.js -- and by 2026-08-22 every one of them was false.
Notion, six chat platforms, two container registries and a model host had
arrived since the list was written, and a decision recorded in one prose
file cannot propagate to eight others. The widget ended up asserting the
OPPOSITE of the governing document.
So: prose points HERE. It does not restate this. If you are about to write
a sentence that counts the paths, link this file instead.
connectors/test/egress.test.mjs fails on any host literal in tracked source
that is not listed below. That is the enforcement -- it fires on the commit
that opens the socket, which is when ui/AGENTS.md's ordering rule says to
catch it ('get this exemption text updated BEFORE the first commit that
opens a non-loopback socket -- not after'). That rule was broken at least
four times before this file existed.
ADDING A PATH: add it here, in the same commit as the code, with a real
`decision` -- and if no real decision exists, write UNRECORDED rather than
inventing one -- never-fabricate binds this file too.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO: it records what the code CAN reach. It is not
a claim that each path is justified, and it is not consent. Read `decision`
on each entry.
WHAT `decision` MEANS HERE. In the private repository it recorded that the
owner had approved a path, and 'UNRECORDED' flagged one nobody had signed
off. Open source has no single owner, so it now records WHY a path exists
and WHO opens it: a user-enabled source, a build-time download, a link
handed to the user's browser. If you add a path, say which.
SCOPE. This ledger describes THIS repository. One entry was removed when the
code was extracted for open source: the outbound iMessage lane, which was the
courier's send path and is not here. A ledger that over-declares is as
misleading as one that under-declares — it invites a reader to believe a
capability exists.
2026-08-24. The marketing site MOVED INTO this repository, at site/. It reaches

EIGHT hosts, seven of them declared below under kind `website`. The seventh is huggingface.co, which already had an entry as a `model-asset` -- one host, two contexts, so filtering by kind alone under-counts the site. They were
removed on 2026-08-22 when site/ was a separate artifact; that sentence is now
false and has been rewritten rather than left standing. connectors/test/
egress.test.mjs promoted `site` out of ROOTS_ELSEWHERE and into ROOTS in the
same commit, which is what its floor test exists to force: a root that arrives
unscanned fails the suite. Note what these entries are NOT -- no process in
this repo opens them. They are what a VISITOR's browser fetches or follows.

2026-08-23. The login-webview kind was DEFINED here and had ZERO entries, while the in-app login had been navigating Meta's hosts since it shipped. The tripwire could not see them: allowedSuffixes was a Swift array of BARE host strings ('instagram.com'), and the scan matches https?://host. So a host list that is a fence rather than a URL is invisible to it -- worth knowing, because a fence is exactly a list of places the code can go. The five entries added here close that, and connect/test/bridgePolicy.test.mjs now asserts each platform's loginUrl is inside its own fence.

2026-08-31. First model egress, and _the_claim narrowed with it. It used to read: 'HAZLIE SENDS NO CORPUS TEXT TO A CLOUD MODEL. All reasoning and narration happen locally, on loopback llama-server instances.' The owner-reviewed frontier handoff (kind frontier-client) replaced that absolute: answers still begin locally and no raw row, quote or hidden context is ever attached, but text the owner reviews and approves now leaves through installed official provider clients. The old sentence is kept here, struck by this paragraph rather than deleted, so nobody re-derives it as still current.

2026-09-07. Second api.anthropic.com entry, new kind public-lookup (L5 step 6). The installed claude client engines.mjs already drives headless (the frontier-client row above, person-page building) is now ALSO driven headless with WebSearch as its one enabled tool, to look a person up on the public web using only public identifiers the owner's corpus already holds. Same host, same installed binary, a materially different tool grant and prompt content -- so it gets its own kind and its own decision rather than being folded into the existing row, per this file's own rule that duplicate hosts in `paths` are fine (declaredHosts is a Set) but a row's `decision` must describe what THAT invocation actually does.

2026-09-08. The api.anthropic.com frontier-client row above named ONE producer -- "person-page builder, L5 step 4" -- while THREE ride it. createEngine defaults to claude-cli whenever the binary resolves, and the sweep (THEM/ME excerpts of new lines plus meeting titles) and the card drafter (page lines, the person's last quoted line, owner tone samples) both reach it through the same default with no config set. `grep -c sweep ops/EGRESS.json` was 0. The HOST was declared, so the literal-host tripwire stayed quiet by design -- and this file's own rule is that a row's `decision` must describe what THAT invocation actually does, so two producers riding a row written for a third is exactly the drift the file exists to prevent. Note also that api.anthropic.com appears as a URL literal in no product file at all: the socket is opened by the spawned binary, so the tripwire is structurally blind to this whole feature and only the ledger text can carry it. connectors/test/egress.test.mjs grew a test that greps the ledger for each producer's module path in the same commit, because a claim nothing checks is the state this file was created out of.

_kinds.api: the daemon or server opens this socket itself, on a timer or on demand
_kinds.bridge: a local container holds a standing authenticated session to this platform
_kinds.registry: container image pull, at install/upgrade time only
_kinds.login-webview: an in-app WKWebView loads this so the owner can log in; cookies are harvested from it
_kinds.user-browser-link: NOT this program's egress -- a link handed to the owner's own browser
_kinds.website: a host the public marketing site in site/ reaches: a subresource the visitor's browser loads, or a link it hands them. Not the product's egress -- no daemon opens these
_kinds.frontier-client: an installed official provider client receives one user-reviewed prompt on stdin and owns its subscription login and vendor-controlled network stack; the app neither implements its socket nor reads its credential
_kinds.public-lookup: the installed claude client is driven headless, with WebSearch as its one enabled tool, to search the public web for a person the owner already knows using only public identifiers (name, firm, a public handle, a public profile URL) the owner's own corpus already holds; no per-call review box -- the review happens afterward through the PENDING claim queue, same as every other producer here
_kinds.judgment-model: a hosted decision model (TypeSafe Jev) receives structured state derived from the owner's own messages plus typed questions, and returns numbers and closed enums only -- no text; the socket is opened by hermes itself, on a timer, with no per-call review

_the_claim: The narrow claim this system actually keeps, stated once:
ANSWERS BEGIN LOCALLY. HAZLIE NEVER ATTACHES RAW CORPUS ROWS, QUOTES OR
HIDDEN RETRIEVAL CONTEXT TO A CLOUD REQUEST. A frontier handoff sends only
the exact text the user reviews, may edit, and explicitly approves.
That is much narrower than 'nothing leaves this Mac', which is false and
must not be written anywhere. Data leaves on every `api`, `bridge` and
`login-webview` path below, and reviewed prompt text leaves on a
`frontier-client` path. The local answer inside that prompt may contain
private derived facts. ui/server/hermes.mjs keeps the only DB handle; the
provider clients receive no handle, row, quote, hidden snippet or app-held
credential.
AND THE HALF THIS PARAGRAPH DOES NOT COVER, said plainly rather than left
to be inferred from the rows: three producers in the relationship layer
(pages.mjs, sweep.mjs, draft.mjs) and the public lookup (lookup.mjs) drive
the installed claude client HEADLESS, with NO review box, on a timer. The
first three send text derived from the owner's own messages -- THEM/ME
conversation excerpts, meeting titles, a person's last quoted line. So
'a frontier handoff sends only the exact text the user reviews' is true of
the widget's handoff and NOT of those four paths. The owner's 2026-09-07
prototype decision authorizes them; read the api.anthropic.com rows below
for what each one actually sends before quoting the sentence above.

paths.purpose: send one prompt whose complete text the owner reviewed and approved, then receive one answer. chatgpt.com is the root service destination; the installed Codex client may use additional vendor-controlled supporting hosts outside this repository's implementation and literal-host tripwire
paths.credential: owned and refreshed by the installed Codex client through Sign in with ChatGPT; Intaglio never reads, copies or logs it
paths.decision: Owner-directed 2026-08-31. Allowed only after the local answer, through the visible editable review box and a provider-named send button. The process gets a separate empty private working directory, read-only sandbox, no approvals, no app database handle and no inherited API-key variables. Its sibling isolated CODEX_HOME is deleted and rebuilt before every run with only a symlink to Codex's own auth file — client state from earlier handoffs cannot linger — so the model-visible working directory contains no credential and ordinary Codex plugins, hooks, MCP servers, skills, history and config cannot observe the prompt. The exact sent text remains visible as a receipt.

paths.purpose: TWO SHAPES, one host and one installed binary. (a) The widget's frontier handoff: one prompt whose complete text the owner reviewed and approved, then one answer. (b) engines.mjs' createClaudeCliEngine, driven headless with an EMPTY tool set by three producers in the relationship layer, each of which sends text DERIVED FROM THE OWNER'S OWN MESSAGES with no per-call review box -- see `decision` for exactly what each one sends. api.anthropic.com is the root service destination; the installed Claude client may use additional vendor-controlled supporting hosts outside this repository's implementation and literal-host tripwire

paths.decision:
Owner-directed 2026-08-31 for the widget's frontier handoff, under the visible-review boundary described for ChatGPT above: safe mode, empty tool set, no permission prompts, strict empty MCP configuration, empty settings sources, no browser, no session persistence, and the approved prompt on stdin rather than argv. 

OWNER DECISION 2026-09-07 (prototype, recorded verbatim in the session that built it): "use my subscription; privacy when it matters, intelligence where needed". That authorizes the installed claude client to be driven headless by ui/server/relationship/engines.mjs with NO per-call review box, by every producer named below; the review happens afterwards through the PENDING claim queue on the desk, where nothing becomes an accepted fact until the owner decides. It does NOT narrow what leaves, and this row used to name only the first of the three, which is why it is spelled out. WHAT EACH PRODUCER SENDS:

  * pages.mjs (person pages, L5 step 4) -- the person's display name and role, and up to ~6k characters of THEM/ME conversation excerpts pooled from their episodes: real iMessage/WhatsApp/mail body text from the owner's corpus, plus the titles of meetings attended together. gatherPersonContext -> renderPrompt.
  * sweep.mjs (discovery sweep, L5 step 5) -- the same THEM/ME excerpt shape, restricted to lines NEW since that person's cursor, plus the person's name, role and sub-role tags, plus the titles of upcoming calendar meetings attended together. newRowsFor -> renderSweepPrompt. Reachable by hand as `node ui/scripts/sweep-once.mjs --power full --engine claude-cli`, and on the Distiller's timer.
  * draft.mjs (card drafts) -- the person's name, the card and owe kind, days overdue, the owner's own recorded commitment text, the built page lines about that person (model-composed prose), the person's last quoted line verbatim, and owner-authored ME lines as a tone sample. renderPrompt.

So: private message-derived text about third parties leaves on this path, unreviewed per call, on a timer. That is the decision as taken -- it is not softened here, and _the_claim above is narrower than this row for exactly that reason ("reviewed prompt text" covers (a) and not (b)). The isolation posture is unchanged from (a) and is what the decision rests on: empty tool set, no MCP, empty settings sources, no browser, no session persistence, prompt on stdin, no database handle, no app-held credential. Revisit before this leaves the house.

paths.component: ui/server/relationship/jev.mjs createJev -> POST /v1/systemone (the only module that opens this socket); driven by the relationship layer's judgment call sites named in `evidence`
paths.purpose: The reconnect card's JUDGMENT layer: which of a person's own lines is worth quoting (a score per candidate line), how the last conversation ended (warm/neutral/bad), how professional and how close the relationship is (two scores) with relatives/romantic flags, whether the owner would want a reminder now, and -- in later commits -- a yes/no prefilter before the local claim distiller, a pick among code-extracted sub-role/firm options in the sweep, and a pick among verbatim lines for person-page sections. Jev generates no text: every answer is a probability, a score or one of the options this code supplied.
paths.credential: a TypeSafe API key the owner placed at ~/.hazlie/secrets/typesafe-api-key.txt (0600; TYPESAFE_API_KEY may override for tests), read by connectors/lib/secrets.mjs readSecretLine, sent as a bearer header, never logged and never in argv
paths.decision: OWNER DECISION 2026-09-20, recorded in the session that built it, in plainer words than it was said: the privacy promise that excerpt-sending features stay off until turned on is dropped for judgments -- this is about the value of the card, and judgments are ON by default whenever a key is present, with no consent toggle. What leaves, unreviewed and on a timer: a code-built `personState` bundle (LinkedIn title/company/industry, channels, message volume/balance/span and meeting counts rendered as WORDS, recency as words, the last 8 direct lines each clipped to 160 characters, one long line from the other person per year up to 6) and, for the quote judgment, up to 12 of the other person's recent lines; for the distiller prefilter, the owner's and the other person's lines of an episode. The Claude toggle in engines.mjs is unchanged. TypeSafe's published policy 2026-09-20: no training on inputs; retention per their DPA; zero-data-retention is an enterprise option not in force here. Measured before shipping (54 owner-judged cards, 2026-09-20): structured state lifted 'would the owner want this reminder' from AUC 0.58 to 0.72; kind is read as two axes because a four-way label was wrong for friends the owner also works with.

paths.purpose: search the public web for a person the owner already knows, using only public identifiers the owner's own corpus already holds (display name, firm/company, a public handle already in the corpus, a public LinkedIn profile URL), then receive a search-grounded answer. The search itself executes on Anthropic's side; this repo opens no other socket for it and stores no fetched page, only the search result's own quoted text and the URL it cited

paths.decision: Owner-directed prototype decision, 2026-09-07 (recorded in the session that built it). A second, narrower invocation of the same installed client as the row above: an empty tool set is replaced with exactly one enabled tool (`--tools WebSearch`, which is the EXCLUSIVE available-tool set -- `--allowedTools` is only the auto-approve list and is passed alongside it, never instead of it) and everything else -- empty MCP config, empty settings sources, no permission prompts, no browser, no session persistence, the prompt on stdin never argv -- stays the same isolation posture engines.mjs already uses. The prompt is told nothing about why it is being asked (no message/transcript text, no claim text, no email or phone number, no calendar contents, no person_key, not even that this is for a reconnect) and is built by buildLookupQuery's own input gate, which refuses any field outside that public-identifier allowlist before it reads a single property. No per-call review box -- the review happens afterward through the PENDING claim queue, the same gate every other producer in this system uses. Revisit before this leaves the house. Since 2026-09-09 a lookup may run up to 4 searches (was 2) so a change can be corroborated across independent sources; the CLI is bounded with --max-turns 5 and the stream-read count enforces the cap; the daily cap of 20 lookups is unchanged, so worst-case search volume doubled.

paths.purpose: Slack's web client, which the login window walks to after a successful sign-in because it is where the session's client token lives.
paths.credential: the owner's own Slack session, already established by the sign-in they just completed in that window.
paths.decision: Already covered by the slack.com entry in substance — the fence matches by suffix and app.slack.com is inside it — and listed separately because the tripwire reads literals, and because the reason this particular subdomain is named in source deserves to be findable. Slack's sign-in ends on an interstitial offering to launch the desktop app; that page holds no token, so the window walks to the web client once, after the required cookies prove the sign-in worked. Not a workaround for a failed login: it is the last step the owner would otherwise have to know to take, and one of them sat on that page with nothing to press (2026-08-26).

paths.purpose: Google's OAuth sign-in, when the owner chooses "Sign In With Google" on Slack's own login page inside the bridge login window.

paths.decision: Slack's login page offers email, Google and Apple, and the window's fence allowed only slack.com -- so the Google button reached slack.com/signin/oauth/google/start and the next hop was cancelled with no error, which reads as a dead button (owner, 2026-08-26). Allowed because it IS Slack's sign-in, not a detour from it. Measured with a fenceless probe that clicked the button and logged every main-frame host; the enumeration stops at Google's "Email or phone" screen, because going further means typing an address and a password, which is the owner's to do. A later 2FA hop through a host not listed here will die the same silent way, and the fix is to measure that hop and name it, never to widen this to google.com.
